extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals (PRSA members and practitioners)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for ethical practice in public relations, as maintained and interpreted by the PRSA Board of Ethics and Professional Standards (BEPS), including the PRSA Code of Ethics, Ethical Standards Advisories (ESAs), case studies, and practical checklists.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRSA Code of Ethics (core principles)
rubrics_metrics.description: The PRSA Code of Ethics sets out principles and guidelines that uphold the core values of the ethical practice of public relations, including advocacy, honesty, loyalty, professional development and objectivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Code provides examples of malpractice, inappropriate and unethical behavior and is intended to inspire, educate and motivate ethical behavior. The 2000 revision shifted emphasis from enforcement to education/inspiration; each provision includes examples to help identify misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Unethical / Improper / Malpractice behaviors
rubrics_metrics.description: Behaviors identified as unethical, improper or malpractice include: a threat to the ethical practice of public relations; behaviors inappropriate or inconsistent with the Code; behaviors disruptive or that undermine ethical practices; practices and behaviors destructive to the reputation of practitioners, the profession or society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories are used to warn and teach members how to avoid improper behavior; the Code provides illustrative examples rather than relying on sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical Standards Advisories (ESAs) — general
rubrics_metrics.description: ESAs are considered direct extensions of the PRSA Code and have the same force and effect as any provision within the PRSA Code. They analyze current practice issues and challenges and provide guidance to deal with new situations as they arise in daily PR practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ESAs are designed to keep the Code timely through a formal process; BEPS solicits member input for ESA topics. ESAs provide practitioner guidance rather than punitive rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: ESA: Disclosure (2018)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance addressing disclosure obligations in public relations practice (Disclosure, 2018).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As an ESA, this advisory interprets Code principles for disclosure contexts and explains practitioner responsibilities for transparent disclosure; ESAs carry the same force as Code provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: ESA: Ethics and Social Media (2015)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on ethical issues arising from the use of social media by practitioners and clients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers practitioner conduct, transparency, representation, and disclosure when using social platforms; intended to apply Code principles to emerging social media scenarios.

rubrics_metrics.name: ESA: Disclosure and Transparency in Native Advertising and Sponsored Content (Sept. 2014)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on disclosure and transparency requirements specific to native advertising and sponsored content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interprets Code obligations for clear labeling and truthful representation of paid or sponsored content so audiences can distinguish advertising from editorial.

rubrics_metrics.name: ESA: Deceptive Online Practices and Misrepresentation of Organizations and Individuals (Rev. June 2012)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance addressing deceptive online practices and online misrepresentation of organizations and individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies Code standards to online behavior, emphasizing truthfulness and prohibiting misrepresentation or covert manipulation online.

rubrics_metrics.name: ESA: Illegal Recordings (March 2011)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance concerning the ethical use and handling of recordings obtained illegally or without proper consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies practitioner responsibilities to avoid, disclose, or appropriately handle unlawfully obtained recordings in light of Code principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: ESA: Ethical Use of Interns (February 2011)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on the ethical treatment and use of interns within PR organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses fair labor practices, appropriate assignments, supervision, and avoiding exploitation; interprets Code obligations toward professional development and fair treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: ESA: Plagiarism (September 2010)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on plagiarism and proper attribution in public relations work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains expectations for originality, acknowledgment of sources, and avoiding misappropriation of others' work in accordance with Code standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: ESA: Looking the Other Way (August 2010)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance regarding the ethical implications of ignoring wrongdoing or failing to act when confronted with unethical behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses practitioner responsibilities to report, resist, or address unethical acts instead of passively allowing them to continue.

rubrics_metrics.name: ESA: Expropriation of the Intellectual Property of Others (February 2010)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on avoiding misappropriation or theft of others' intellectual property in PR practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers appropriate use of third-party IP, licensing, attribution, and respect for proprietary materials per Code obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: ESA: Use of Video News Releases as a Public Relations Tool (October 2009)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on ethical considerations when producing and distributing video news releases (VNRs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses transparency, disclosure, and representation when distributing VNR content to news outlets and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: ESA: Questionable Environmental Claims and Endorsements (Greenwashing) (October 2009)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on environmental claims and endorsements to prevent misleading 'greenwashing' in communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies Code principles to ensure accuracy and substantiation of environmental claims and endorsements.

rubrics_metrics.name: ESA: Pay for Play (October 2009)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance addressing arrangements where payment influences placement, coverage, or endorsements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes disclosure and avoidance of deceptive practices where financial arrangements could mislead audiences about editorial independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: ESA: Engaging in the Use of Deceptive Practices While Representing Front Groups (Rev. October 2008)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance prohibiting deceptive practices when practitioners represent front groups or disguised advocacy entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interprets Code prohibitions on misrepresentation and deceptive identity or sponsorship practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: ESA: Overstating Charges, Fees and/or Compensation (rev. August 2007)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on truthful representation of fees, charges, and compensation structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directs practitioners to avoid misrepresenting costs or financial arrangements to clients or the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: ESA: Disclosure by Expert Commentators and Professional Spokespersons of Payments or Financial Interests (April 2005)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance requiring disclosure of payments or financial interests by expert commentators and professional spokespersons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures audiences are informed about potential conflicts of interest that could bias commentary or endorsements.

rubrics_metrics.name: ESA: Telling the Truth, Especially in War Time (January 2005)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance reinforcing truthfulness in communications, with special attention to the heightened stakes during wartime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reaffirms Code obligations to avoid misinformation and to disclose relevant context when public safety and public interest are involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: ESA: Reporting Unethical Behavior or Unprofessional Performance (Nov. 2004)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on responsibilities and procedures for reporting unethical behavior or unprofessional performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains mechanisms for bringing concerns to BEPS and the expectation that practitioners act to address serious ethical breaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: ESA: Disclosure of Employment Status of Client-Based PR Agency Staff (May 2004)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on disclosure obligations related to the employment status of agency staff assigned to client accounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses transparency about who is speaking or acting on behalf of clients and agencies to prevent misleading impressions of independence or affiliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics Case Studies and Discussion Guides (topics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Collection of ethics case studies and discussion guides covering issues such as safeguarding confidences; looking the other way; conflicts of interest; competition; enhancing the profession; ethical decision making; dilemmas and moral questions; matrix of ethical dilemmas; content, digital and organizational issues (illegal recordings, plagiarism, expropriating IP, free flow of information, disclosure of information, deceptive online practices, representing front groups, ethical use of interns).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case studies are available as downloadable materials with discussion guides to help practitioners and educators explore real-world ethical dilemmas and proper responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: BEPS Handbook: practical checklists and warning signs
rubrics_metrics.description: BEPS Handbook includes practical tools such as 'Eight Ethics Questions to Ask Yourself Before Acting', 'Six Statements That Should Warn You of a Potential Ethical Violation', 'Six Indications That Your Company Has an Ethical Culture', 'Eight Ethics Quotes', and 'Six Practical Recommendations for Building Employer Branding'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These checklist-style items are intended as immediate decision-making aids and diagnostics to help practitioners identify and prevent ethical problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision to End Sanctioning; focus on education/inspiration
rubrics_metrics.description: PRSA ended identifying and sanctioning Code violators in 2000 and shifted to a Code that focuses on education, inspiration and motivating ethical behavior rather than enforcement and punishment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale includes limited enforceability of voluntary codes, legal risks and costs of enforcement, members' reluctance to report colleagues, and procedural limitations; the Code therefore emphasizes examples and education rather than punitive sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations of PRSA enforcement as a voluntary organization
rubrics_metrics.description: As a voluntary organization PRSA cannot subpoena evidence, authorize sanctions, or enforce beyond voluntary participation; organizations empowered to sanction typically derive that power from statute, licensure, or governmental authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because PRSA lacks legal enforcement authority, it focuses on voluntary practice standards, education, promotion of voluntary compliance, and establishing ethical obligations rather than formal punishments.

rubrics_metrics.name: BEPS communications and member process
rubrics_metrics.description: BEPS is a volunteer board that responds to member inquiries and builds the ESA library based on practitioner input; members can email BEPS or inform BEPS about particular concerns via a form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BEPS will make every effort to respond in a timely manner; members are asked to allow three weeks before re-contacting BEPS. Member input helps shape ESAs and resources.
